newsitem.title: USA: Iowa gaming board may pull Prairie Meadows license.
newsitem.headline: Iowa gaming board may pull Prairie Meadows license.

text.p: Iowa Racing and Gaming Commission Administrator Jack Ketterer said Friday the commission may pull the operating license of a profitable publicly owned race track and casino.

The commission voted 5-0 on Thursday to have staff members prepare a notice asking the Racing Association of Central Iowa to show why its license to operate the Altoona facility should not be revoked "for failure to be the true owner of the enterprise," Ketterer said.
Commissioners are expected to approve the notice at their August meeting and set a hearing on the license revocation for Sept. 18 if licensing issues are not resolved before then, Ketterer said.
Prairie Meadows Race Track had stood on the verge of bankruptcy when Polk County acted as underwriter of bonds to keep it afloat.
The installation of slot machines in 1995 made the track profitable, allowing Polk County to retire the debt and project a profit for fiscal 1998.
Polk County owns the "bricks and mortar" at Prairie Meadows, but state law bars the county from holding the operating license for the facility, Ketterer noted.
Commissioners believe the operating lease improperly moves profits to Polk County and leaves doubt as to the true operator of the facility, however, Ketterer said.

"Some of the (lease) provisions were approved with the understanding that they were required by bond counsel on behalf of bondholders to protect funds generated out of the race track and casino," Ketterer said.
Polk County spokesman Phil Roeder said supervisors intend to continue negotiating with the racing association and the two sides are "closer than not" to an agreement.

Supervisors are now considering selling the facility appraised at $160 million to a private developer. A county-commissioned study reported that Prairie Meadows could be worth as much as $294 million to a private developer that would likely add slot machines.
